Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Power Utilities Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Power Utilities' Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; and Emma Rodriguez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by strong operational performance in our generation fleet, continued growth in our renewable energy portfolio, effective cost management, progress on our infrastructure investments, successful integration of the Riverton CCGT Phase II expansion, and advancement of our Powering Tomorrow program.

Let me provide some more detail on these six key aspects, starting with our strong operational performance. This quarter, we delivered standout results with adjusted EBITDA of $1.15 billion, up 14% year-over-year and 5% above our guidance midpoint. This came amid robust load growth, disciplined cost management, and strategic execution across our diversified fleet. Total net generation hit 28.5 TWh, a 9% increase year-over-year, supported by 4.2% weather-normalized load growth in our core areas. Our merchant exposure in ERCOT and MISO really shone, with realized spark spreads at $28 per MWh, exceeding forward curves due to strong summer demand from data centers and EVs. In PJM, our 2.5 GW of combined-cycle gas turbines, including the upgraded Liberty Creek units with GE 7HA.03 tech, posted a fleet-wide equivalent availability factor of 95.8%, up from 93.2% last year. That reliability helped us secure $450 million in capacity payments, making up 22% of regulated revenue.

On renewables, we reached a milestone with the 450 MW Desert Sun solar-plus-storage project in ERCOT's South zone going commercial. It includes 200 MWh of Tesla Megapack 2XL batteries and is backed by a 15-year PPA with a hyperscale tech customer at $42 per MWh weighted average strike, lifting renewable adjusted EBITDA margins to 68%. Year-to-date, we've added 850 MW of renewables, 20% ahead of our 2024 target of 2 GW, with IRRs averaging 12.5% after IRA PTC adjustments. We also inked three big PPAs totaling 1.2 GW: a 600 MW offshore wind offtake with a Mid-Atlantic utility at $75 per MWh, hedged against ITC risks; 400 MW solar in SPP with Google under our green electrons product; and 200 MW firming via our 150 MW/600 MWh BESS in California to tackle the duck curve. This pushes our contracted backlog to 85% through 2027, derisking 70% of 2025 EBITDA.

Financially, we optimized the balance sheet with a $1.2 billion green bond at 4.8%, our lowest coupon yet, extending maturities to 7.2 years and locking sub-5% blended rates. We repurchased $300 million in shares under our $2 billion program, retiring 2.1% of shares at $68 average for 15% ROIC. FFO to debt rose to 18.2%, putting us in the upper quartile versus peers like NextEra and Dominion. Operationally, O&M per MWh fell 8% to $4.25 thanks to our AI predictive maintenance platform with Siemens Energy, rolled out to 80% of gas assets, cutting forced outages 22% with digital twins and edge computing. Renewables saw drone inspections at our 300 MW Wind Horizon farm in Texas Panhandle, slashing cleaning costs 35% and lifting yield 2.2%. In Texas, ERCOT prices hit $250 per MWh in Heat Dome 2.0, with our 1.8 GW gas fleet at full dispatch for $180 million uplift. PJM's RPM auction cleared high at $45 per kW-year for 2025/26, adding $250 million for baseload, and CAISO storage arbitrage yielded 25% returns.

Challenges included extreme weather like Hurricane Beryl, costing $45 million uninsured in opex from outages and vegetation management, though our hardened grid limited downtime to under 2 hours per event versus industry 8+. Fuel costs rose 11% quarter-over-quarter to $3.25 per MMBtu Henry Hub, dragging EBITDA $30 million despite 70% collars. Supply chains delayed our 300 MW Forge Wind in Oklahoma 45 days on blade shortages, like issues at Orsted and Vestas, with panel logistics up 15%. Regulatory hits like FERC Order 2023 added $20 million in queue studies, CPUC NEM 3.0 squeezed community solar 10%, and EPA NOx rules cost $15 million on legacy coal. Curtailment in ERCOT reached 12%, costing $25 million, and gas basis in Appalachia widened. Macro pressures raised AFS losses $50 million on debt and cyber investments to $8 million. But these are transitory; we've pre-bought $500 million inventory and locked multi-year deals with First Solar and GE Vernova. Q3 guidance is $1.05 to $1.12 billion EBITDA, with 2 GW renewables COD by year-end, accelerating BESS to 1 GW by 2025 at 75% contracted.

Next, our continued growth in renewables ties directly into progress on strategic initiatives and long-term goals under our Powering Tomorrow strategy, launched in 2022, with four pillars: clean energy transition, grid modernization, electrification growth, and disciplined capital allocation. We're on track for 50% carbon-free by 2030 and net-zero Scope 1/2 by 2045, per IRA and SEC rules. In Q2, we added 450 MW solar PV in the Southeast, including 250 MW Phase II at Sunny Ridge Solar Farm in Georgia at $28 per MWh LCOE, 15% under hurdle, with 20-year PPAs. Year-to-date, 1.2 GW renewables brings clean capacity to 8.5 GW, 32% of our 26 GW portfolio, ahead of 30% target. Storage progress includes 300 MW/1,200 MWh BESS at Texas Wind Plains in ERCOT at 92% efficiency, capturing $150 per MWh spreads in July heat. We have 2.5 GW renewables and 1 GW storage advancing, 80% contracted to Google, Microsoft hyperscalers. Nuclear renaissance with NuScale FEED for SMRs at South Carolina coal site targets 300 MW by 2030 under $60 per MWh LCOE. Carbon intensity down 18% to 350 gCO2/kWh, on pace for 65% cut from 2005 by 2030.

In Southeast SERC/Entergy, solar curtailment down 5% post-$150 million upgrades; ERCOT at 99.8% reliability, wind CF 38%; CAISO hydro at 12% ROE. Grid pillar: $400 million YTD in AMI/ADMS for 85% smart meters, cutting Florida peak demand 12%; microgrids with Tesla Megapacks won $50 million DOE grants. Load forecast 3.5% CAGR to 2030 from 2 GW data centers, 500 MW EV hubs. Electrification: 1 GW wheeling at 15% IRRs, 10-year green H2 PPA ramping to 100 MW, Apex Home VPPs with 150,000 customers curtailing 200 MW for $20 million payments at 95% AI accuracy. Capital pillar: $2.8 billion of $5-6 billion 2024 capex, 70% regulated at 10.5% ROE; FCF 95%, 4.2% dividend, $500 million buybacks; ROIC 9.8% to 10.5% by 2026 via IRA $250 million EBITDA. Reaffirming 6-8% EPS CAGR to 2030, rate base to $45 billion at 7%. Risks mitigated: panel delays via 3 GW First Solar contracts, rates with 65% fixed debt at 4.1%. Opportunities: 5 GW AI loads by 2028, 3 GW PJM bids at $40/kW-month. Clean EBITDA up 15% YoY, positioning us as Southeast transition leader.

On effective cost management, our EPS performance highlights this strength. We reported GAAP EPS of $1.42, up 18% from $1.20 last year; adjusted $1.35, beating guidance $1.28-$1.32 midpoint and consensus $1.30 by 4%, eighth straight beat. Revenues $2.85 billion, up 12%, from 15% wholesale price surge. ERCOT 4.2 GW peakers/500 MW BESS saw $85 per MWh on-peak LMPs on 2.5 GW data center adds; 92% capacity factor, 85% hedged at $45 per MWh. PJM 1.8 GW nuclear at Susquehanna 105% delivered 4.2 TWh at $28 per MWh spreads, up 22% on $240/MW-day auctions. Regulated Midwest utility sales up 4% post-ICC settlement adding $150 million revenue. Opex $1.12 billion flat despite inflation via digital twins cutting outages 22%; fuel down 10% to $320 million at $2.40 Henry Hub. D&A up 14% to $420 million on $1.2 billion capex like 300 MW solar-storage in CA. Interest up 8% to $180 million at 4.2% blended, offset by $120 million buybacks adding $0.09 EPS. Tax 22% with IRA PTCs. 2024 guidance $5.10-$5.30, 2025 $5.60-$5.90 or 10-12% growth from 1.5 GW COD, 15% EPS from battery stake, NY CLCPA. Hybrids 65% low-carbon, $15 billion five-year capex to 85% renewables/nuclear.

Progress on infrastructure investments aligns with our capex plan. Affirming 2024 capex at $11.2 billion, up 8%, 18% of $62 billion year-end rate base for 6-8% EPS growth. Five-year $58 billion at 7% CAGR: 45% generation ($5.0B), 40% T&D ($4.5B), 15% customer ($1.7B). Renewables 55% of gen capex: 1.2 GW COD like 450 MW Sweetwater Solar at $35/MWh 25-year PPA, 12% IRR. Pipeline 2.8 GW: 1.1 GW Horizon Wind+Storage 65% complete with GE turbines/Fluence BESS, IRA cuts equity 35%, COD Q4 2025; 600 MW Palmetto Solar groundbreaking. 200 MW/800 MWh iron-air BESS pilot in Ohio permitting. Thermal: $800 million peakers/nuclear; 1.2 GW Meadowbrook CCGT repower to 64% efficiency H2-ready; Crystal River 50 MW uprate to 93% CF; NuScale SMR MOU. T&D record $4.5B: 75% of $1.2B Southeast hardener with 5,000 miles underground/SF6-free; PJM $900 million reconductoring. Southeast $4.8B 50% renewables, 4% load; Midwest $3.2B MISO queue; ERCOT $2.0B merchant. Tailwinds: IRA $1.1B credits, 2.5% peak CAGR, 70% PPAs. Headwinds: 15% steel/transformers, mitigated by 70/30 financing, $2.5B ATM. $650 million AFUDC, 95% on-budget/schedule.

The successful integration of our Riverton CCGT Phase II expansion followed key regulatory wins across states. In Pennsylvania PJM, Q2 base case settled for $240 million on $12.4 billion rate base (6.2% growth) at 10.1% ROE/51% equity, 84% of $285 million ask, with three-year plan for AMI (95%) and EV ports. Boosts 2024 EPS $0.18. Illinois MISO formula approved 98% of $420 million on $15.7 billion (5.8% growth) at 9.8% ROE, decoupling for 1.2 TWh EE. Missouri SPP settled $152 million of $175 million ask (87%) at 10.2% ROE/50% equity, moratorium to 2026. Texas PUCT pending $310 million on $9.2 billion for hardening, 90%+ likely. FERC true-up $65 million refund at 10.0% ROE. 92% recovery YTD supports 6-7% rate base CAGR; PBR pilots hit 99.97% reliability. 2025 filings: Illinois $550 million, Missouri update, Texas CCN. Risks: ROE compression, clawbacks; 85% regulated mix helps.

Finally, advancing Powering Tomorrow drove rate base growth to $27.4 billion end-September, up 7.2% from $25.6 billion Q3 2023, 14th straight 6%+ quarter vs. peer 5.1%. Equity rate base $18.2 billion up 6.8%, fully earned at 10.35% Florida ROE, 85% AFUDC at 4.8%. 2024 capex $3.2 billion up 12%, 72% T&D: $1.45 billion modernization like $450 million Panhandle 345-kV ($320 million CWIP), ERCOT $280 million HVDC 75% complete +1,200 MW. Clean transition $900 million: 650 MW solar like 300 MW Sunny Oaks ($45 million 45X), 200 MW/800 MWh Cypress Peak BESS $180 million; renewables 42% of 12 GW. Gen optimization $575 million: retire 400 MW coal Plant Harlan, $350 million Riverton CCGT +550 MW >62% efficiency. Customer $285 million: 450,000 AMI, dynamic pricing -8% peak; 2.4% Southeast load, ERCOT 1.2 GW industrial. Tailwinds: Florida 10.35%/52.5% equity, Texas 10.25% CWIP, Georgia 10.5% pending; 2.8% sales, 4.2% debt. Headwinds: 6% steel mitigated 80% EPC locks, rates via $1.2B ATM $52/share, $400 million coal reserves offset $1.1B new. 2025-2029 $16.5 billion for 7.5% growth to $38 billion. Ahead of peers via ERCOT/CWIP.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Reynolds to discuss the financials.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. For the third quarter, we reported earnings per share of $1.35 adjusted and revenue of $2.85 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $3.2 billion, primarily focused on transmission and distribution modernization and clean energy transition projects. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate 6-8% EPS growth through 2030.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our combined-cycle gas turbine power plants due to the implementation of AI-powered predictive maintenance. This has resulted in a 10% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 20%.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the long-duration energy storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the ERCOT market.

Emma Rodriguez: Thank you, David. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed an advanced zero-trust cybersecurity framework to enhance our defenses against cyber threats.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Michael, Lisa, David, and Emma. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for rate base growth?

Johnathan Hale: Certainly, John. As we highlighted, rate base hit $27.4 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year, with equity at $18.2 billion growing 6.8%, fully earned via AFUDC. Drivers include $3.2 billion capex: 45% T&D like Panhandle project adding $320 million CWIP, ERCOT HVDC; 28% clean like Sunny Oaks solar and Cypress BESS; 18% gen swaps maintaining neutrality; 9% customer AMI/EV. Tailwinds from ROE settlements giving 150 bps premium, 2.8% load, efficient financing. Headwinds like inflation locked via contracts, rates via ATM, retirements offset. Five-year plan to $38 billion at 7.5%, ahead of peers.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: What is your outlook for CAPEX?

Michael Reynolds: Great question, Maria. 2024 at $11.2 billion affirmed, five-year $58 billion at 7% CAGR: renewables heavy like Horizon 1.1 GW, Palmetto 600 MW; thermal reliability; T&D record highs post-storms. Positions for 5-7% rate base growth, 85% recovery, IRA tailwinds. On track with strong execution.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim: How are you mitigating risks related to regulatory rate cases?

Lisa Chen: Absolutely, David. We've seen 92% recovery YTD across PA, IL, MO, TX filings, with constructive outcomes like PA three-year plan, IL decoupling, MO moratorium. Forward PBR, strong relationships, 85% regulated mix derisk. 2025 filings prepared, balancing with merchant growth.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning Apex Power Utilities for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in Apex Power Utilities.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
